heading: Before taking an S corporation distribution, assemble the basis file
body:
A company bank balance does not establish how much an owner can receive without tax. The IRS distinguishes shareholder stock basis from debt basis, and a Schedule K-1 does not by itself tell the owner the taxable portion of a distribution. Use the book to understand the concepts, then bring a reconciled record to the person preparing the shareholder return.

Build a transaction history the preparer can follow

Collect the prior-year basis schedule, current and corrected K-1s, evidence of stock purchases or capital contributions, distribution dates and amounts, and records of direct shareholder loans and repayments. Identify which amounts are supported and which still require reconstruction. Keep stock and debt activity in separate schedules; combining them can hide the question the adviser needs to resolve.

For a fictional shareholder who received $45,000, the fact that the corporation had $100,000 in the bank does not establish distribution treatment. Nor should a loan balance be added automatically to stock basis to justify the payment. Ask the preparer to show the relevant basis computation, ordering rules, and any further limitations before treating the transfer as resolved.

Close the loop with bookkeeping and payroll

Confirm that owner transfers were recorded consistently as wages, distributions, reimbursements, loan activity, or another supported category. A bookkeeping label does not determine the final tax result. If records disagree, assign one person to reconcile them and retain the explanation used for the return. Review the IRS stock and debt basis guidance with the applicable year’s forms and professional advice.

Prepare the right file for the owner conversation

Start with the year-end S corporation basis reconciliation when the open question concerns the shareholder's permanent records and the return-preparation handoff. For the separate owner-pay discussion, use the reasonable-compensation workpaper guide to organize role descriptions, supporting records, and questions for the reviewer. Give each unresolved item an owner and keep the final explanation with the applicable year. These companion guides help prepare the discussion; they do not establish a compensation amount or approve a distribution.
